INV: Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency and, separately, per ownership tag: client lines and company lines each balance on their own (restated v5.9 — the per-owner rule of D46, until now stated only inside invariant 16).
Ledger tables are append-only; corrections are reversing transactions.

Custody in NPL’s own wallet is allowed in four cases only: a collection on a deal with an approved REROUTE before conversion; the balance of a reroute after conversion while it waits to be forwarded; a leg whose PARTNER_CONFIG is an own desk (D23, the NPL-GR project); or a collection on a wallet with role collection_bridge, which is forwarded to the leg’s partner as a hop (a SETTLEMENT_LINE to the partner_transit receiver) within the wallet’s custody_max_hours (D40). CL.OWN.*.HELD is debited by nothing else; the custody aging view reports all three and is the standing control.

Settle to the residual: under settlement_policy = to_zero a SETTLEMENT pays the balance rounded by the pair’s option and leaves only the rounding residual (dust stays client money; a round-up is NPL’s cost — D25); under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project’s exposure cap (Q5, Q8).
Priced once, per leg: a leg’s pricing fields are write-once after priced_at; a re-quote is a new leg or a new deal group.

Partner fixed at quote, per leg: partner_pair_id / partner_entity_id change only through an approved REROUTE. A collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity (v5.1, D15). Its kind must match the leg’s collection_method — wallet for crypto, bank for bank, no endpoint for cash (v5.2, D19). A COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint; a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).

Entitlement conservation, over postings: Σ GROUP_ENTITLEMENT over a project’s groups = the balance of CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE = Σ COLLECTED + Σ HELD + Σ DUE + Σ SHORTFALL + MAKEGOOD − Σ CREDIT, per currency, after every transaction — because every transaction balances per owner and every PAYABLE line carries a receiver_group_id. Return and hop legs preserve it by inheriting the parent leg’s group (D13); a payout to a group-less receiver carries the paying leg’s group (D17) (restated, D46 amendment).

Destination approval precedes collection: a quote-first deal cannot leave Inquiry unless at least one account in the entitled group has a DESTINATION_APPROVAL in state approved with the chosen partner.

Approver ≠ initiator on every APPROVAL, and the approver’s ROLE has may_approve for the action in ROLE_RIGHT while the initiator’s has may_initiate; Operations never receives derived-economics fields (ROLE.sees_economics) (restated v5.4, D44).
Every balance shown anywhere is a sum over postings or deals.
A collect-first deal requires an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry for its sender and group (Q1).
A return leg pays the sender_return RECEIVER linked to the parent leg’s sender, unless a Management-approved exception with a reason names another approved receiver.
The failed forward line is reversed before a return leg opens, so entitlement and balance are correct at the return conversion.
A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a balance conversion.
A recovery on a reroute cannot exceed the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE at that partner; the alternate partner’s expected conversion is computed on the net amount forwarded.

Ownership moves between client and company at named events only, and every transaction balances per owner as well as per currency. Client → company: margin recognition at conversion; the client side of an EARNINGS_OFFSET at the to-partner; a forex true-up gain on a line discharging an invoice; the client’s share of a loss, by partial reversal of the make-good. Company → client: a fee NPL absorbs or covers (bank, network, rounding up), a shortfall top-up, a bounce make-whole, a loss make-good; the company side of an EARNINGS_OFFSET at the from-partner; a forex true-up loss. NPL never advances money to a receiver (Q13) (restated, D46 amendment).

Offsets arise only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to a different group, and carry Management approval and tighter aging. A project with one group never has an offset; within a group nothing is tracked beyond an informational tally (v5.0).

A RECEIVER has a group_id if and only if kind = counterparty. Forward legs and the sender allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only. A return leg inherits receiver_group_id from its parent leg; leg n of a route inherits it from leg n−1 (v5.0, D13).
A SETTLEMENT_LINE paying a group-less receiver (sender_return, partner_transit) carries deal_id; the paying leg’s group is a stored fact, never inferred (v5.2, D17).
A FEE_OVERRIDE with its own split has both share columns set and they sum to its pct; with neither set the structure’s proportion applies. The leg stamps the override that priced it (v5.3, D20).

The base tier stamped on a leg is the tier with the highest min_monthly_volume not exceeding the project’s calendar-month volume at quote (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME); a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split into two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions whose amounts sum to amount_in, and its fee parts are the blended sum (v5.3, D21).

Customer-facing figures are derived, never typed: customer_facing_rate = sender_rate ÷ (1 − customer_facing_fee_pct), stamped at quote; the true rates and fee parts are stored beside them and Operations sees the customer-facing pair only (v5.3, D22).

Σ obligation_discharged over a vendor invoice’s released lines never exceeds its amount, and Σ DEAL_GROUP.invoice_amount over a resale invoice’s groups never exceeds its amount. A line that names a vendor invoice names a deal whose group collects the resale invoice that marks it up (vendor_invoice_id), or, outside a reseller project, whose group is on that invoice; the margin line names the resale invoice itself (v5.3 D24; restated D46 amendment).

Rounding is the pair’s configured option — amount_rounding / rounding_unit on payouts, cash_rounding / cash_rounding_unit on the cash amount collected; the residual is signed — a dropped fraction stays client money in the balance, an amount added by rounding up is NPL’s cost posted to EXP_ROUNDING — so every rounding difference has an owner (v5.3, D25).

Σ pct of the share_of_net_markup rules active on one leg ≤ 100 %; the share base is the leg’s fee parts less its partner cost and never includes a partner rebate. A MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL is created and posted by the conversion it arises on; a party_retains accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly (v5.3, D26; restated v5.7, D46).

Rebate income posts only to EARN_REBATE, never to EARN_GROSS; every rebate accrual names the NPLify deal it arises on, is created and posted by that deal’s conversion as a percentage of the amount in the rule’s payout currency, and the partner statement is reconciled against those deals alone (v5.3, D27; restated v5.7, D46 and amendment).

A partner rate version stores the rate as quoted and its direction; the normalised rate is derived (1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ, at the pair’s precision) and is subject to the breach check like any other, so a direction slip freezes the pair instead of pricing a deal (v5.3, D28).

The partner’s cutoff binds two events on pairs that rely on the banking channel. The effective cutoff for a day is the one-day PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE if any, else the weekday rule, else PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time, and is stamped (cutoff_at) on the leg at rate lock and on the settlement at approval. A leg’s conversion_due_date is the lock date when rate_locked_at precedes cutoff_at and the next business day otherwise, and Converting may not start before it; a bank-rail settlement’s execution_due_date follows the same rule from its approval time. The sender’s figures are write-once (invariant 5); the difference between the stamped partner rate and the rate actually used posts to VAR_CUTOFF with component cutoff_timing — NPL absorbs it (v5.3, D29, amended 9 October).

A rate version is unique per partner × pair × day × location; a cash leg carries its cash_location and prices on a version of that location; a cash part is verified only after the partner’s count (counted_at) (v5.3, D30).

A crypto collection names its sending address and, unless the project skips up-front screening, the screening that admitted it; a screening decided accept_alternate may land only on an endpoint whose risk_band is elevated, and no collection exists for a decision of reject unless Finance overrides it (v5.3, D31).

A single_use endpoint or account is referenced by at most one collection or payout line, for the deal it was reserved for, and retires when that reference is verified or confirmed. A LOSS_EVENT’s shares sum to its amount, which never exceeds the amount verified or released. After a collection-side event the part stays verified — NPL’s funds stand in for the lost money — and the client balance never goes below zero; the part moves to reversed only when Management unwinds the deal (v5.3, D32; restated v5.9 to match D46).

A pair whose two currencies are the same is converted at rate 1 like any other pair, so the sender and receiver fee parts are captured at conversion and the balance arithmetic is unchanged (v5.3, D33).

Business days are computed, never assumed: ‘next business day’ for a conversion due date or a settlement execution date skips weekends in the partner’s cutoff_timezone and the partner’s HOLIDAY rows of the matching scope; a reroute with trigger holiday names a day that is a HOLIDAY of scope partner (v5.3, D34).

A quote-first leg leaves Quoted for Sent only when a QUOTE_PACKAGE of its group has sent_at; the package’s content_hash is the leg’s quote_hash and its printed figures equal the group’s customer-facing figures (derived, never typed); freshness runs from the leg’s market snapshot (MARKET_RATE.captured_at) to sent_at within PROJECT.quote_freshness_min, validity from sent_at. Packages are append-only: a re-issue supersedes, a new price is a new deal group. A quote template prints sender-facing fields only (v5.3, D35, D36).

Client-level figures are sums over the client’s projects, never stored (CLIENT_POSITION); when CLIENT.exposure_ceiling is set, Σ PROJECT_BALANCE across the client’s projects may not exceed it — a settlement or a held balance that would breach it needs Management approval, as a project’s own ceiling does (v5.4, D38).

A partner offers only what its record says: a leg’s collection_method, and the method of any settlement through the partner, must be in PARTNER.supported_methods; a wallet endpoint’s network must already exist as an endpoint of that partner’s vehicle before a collection may name it. Adding a method or a network is a Management-approved configuration change (v5.4, D39).

A quote’s validity may be extended any number of times before the validity in force ends, each time by an APPROVAL (extend_quote_validity) recorded as a QUOTE_VALIDITY_EXTENSION that moves effective_valid_until and re-issues the quote package at the same price; Finance approves, Management is added when the new validity passes the partner’s cutoff or the rate version’s expiry. The pricing fields stay write-once (invariant 5). After the validity in force ends, the paths are the grace decision and a new deal group (v5.5, D45; was once-only within grace, D42).

Converted figures are display-only estimates: a REPORTING_VALUE is computed at read time from the latest MARKET_RATE of the platform CURRENCY_PAIR (priced through its PAIR_RATE_SOURCE chain), carries the rate and its time, is flagged when the rate is older than reporting_rate_max_age_min, and is never posted, stored, quoted or settled. The only controls that read it are ceilings stated in the reporting currency (CLIENT.exposure_ceiling); every other limit and every posting stays in its own currency (v5.4, D43).

An expired quote is never revived: the sender gets a new deal group. At the sender’s request that new leg may be priced on the earlier leg’s market rate and partner rate version (rate_reused_from_deal_id) by an approved override (honour_expired_rate, Finance), the automated rate set aside and the grace drift limit not applied; the leg stamps the reused rates as its own, and the difference against the partner’s actual rate at conversion posts to VAR_RATE_HONOUR — NPL’s cost, chosen (v5.5, D45).

A settlement discharges CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE when the partner releases the money (released_at); a SETTLEMENT_RETURN re-raises it for what came back and a short CONFIRMATION for the part not delivered; a full confirmation posts nothing; a hop (partner_transit) posts only when the far side credits and never touches the promise. Every released line ends confirmed, short or returned, and ‘sent, not yet confirmed’ is read from the line, never from an account (v5.7, D46).

CO.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.POOL may be below zero only between a fee NPL absorbed in a currency where it held nothing at that partner and the next conversion there, which then includes NPL’s own USDT converted alongside the client’s (a Conversion with a company part through FX_RESULT); Finance squares every negative pool within the month (v5.7, D46).

Fee parts are percentages of the principal and never compound. Fixed-in (amount_mode fixed_in): principal = amount_in × basis rate; fee_sender_part = principal × sender_pays_pct; fee_receiver_part = principal × receiver_pays_pct; client_net = principal × (1 − sender_pays_pct − receiver_pays_pct). Target-out (amount_mode target_out): the fee is a markup on the target — amount_in = target_out × (1 + sender_pays_pct) ÷ basis rate, then cash-rounded if collected in cash; fee_receiver_part = target_out × receiver_pays_pct; client_net = target_out × (1 − receiver_pays_pct) + any cash-rounding surplus; the sender rate printed is basis rate ÷ (1 + sender_pays_pct) (v5.7, D46; target-out added by the amendment — NPL’s quotes use × (1 + fee), not ÷ (1 − fee)).

An EARNINGS_OFFSET is neutral for the client: from_amount at the from-partner becomes the client’s and to_amount = from_amount ÷ the to-partner’s rate of the day becomes NPL’s, with the client’s promises re-denominated by the same amounts; to_amount never exceeds the client’s unconverted balance at the to-partner, from_amount never exceeds NPL’s pool at the from-partner, and the receivables it recovers are marked recovered_by_offset_id (v5.7, D46).

In NPL-GR the vendor and resale invoices are posted once each, in the invoice currency (RESELL_COST / VENDOR_PAYABLE; RESALE_RECEIVABLE / RESELL_REVENUE), and no later transaction touches RESELL_REVENUE or RESELL_COST in the invoice currency: the reseller revenue is intact by construction. Each group’s collection clears its invoice_amount of RESALE_RECEIVABLE into REMIT_CLAIM; each vendor line clears VENDOR_PAYABLE and REMIT_CLAIM by its obligation_discharged on release; the margin line clears the rest of REMIT_CLAIM; a cash-rounding surplus is NPL-GR’s revenue, posted to RESELL_REVENUE in the currency received, never a forex result; the forex true-up of each instalment posts to VAR_FX_TIMING on the remittance side (v5.7, D46 and amendment; worded per currency in v5.9).

The approver is never the initiator, on the person: APPROVAL.approved_by is refused when its USER.person_ref equals requested_by's, so a user holding two accounts cannot approve their own request (v6.0, Roles & Visibility rule 5a; enforced by a trigger, Appendix C).

An approval is valid only for the record version the approver saw: APPROVAL.record_version must equal the record's current version when the approval is applied, so two approvers at once leave exactly one winner and a changed record is re-approved (v6.0, Lifecycle & Approvals 6a).

At most one open lock per record (partial unique index on record_type, record_id where released_at is null); a lock is released on save or cancel, expires after the project's lock_idle_minutes, or is cleared by Management, and every release is written to AUDIT_LOG (v6.0, D49).

An emergency action takes effect when applied by Finance and is lifted unless Management ratifies it within one business day; ratified_by is never applied_by; every state change is in AUDIT_LOG (v6.0, D47).

Opening entries post once, on the opening date, one transaction per OPENING_ENTRY row (source Opening): company-side balances against CO.NONE.<CCY>.OPENING_BALANCE, client-side balances between the client's jar and the project's promise; OPENING_BALANCE is never posted to again (v6.0, D55, Pattern R).

For every active partner configuration and currency there is one reconciliation row per business day of the parallel run and per month end afterwards; a difference is cleared only by a true-up transaction, never by an edit; a row in state difference_open is on the exception list (v6.0, Pattern Q).

A bank account, bank endpoint or settlement rail is active only with a BANK_ACCOUNT_DETAILS row in status active whose rail matches and whose rail_fields pass the rail's template; a details row is never edited — a change is a new row with supersedes_id and the old row stays; every full read of a details row is in AUDIT_LOG (v6.1, D58).

A sender's source is a bank-details row or a wallet network and address, exactly one of the two: (bank_account_details_id IS NOT NULL) <> (wallet_network IS NOT NULL AND wallet_address IS NOT NULL), and the two wallet columns are set together (Configuration Schema 4).

A leg with hold_kind set accepts no money-moving write: conversion, balance conversion, settlement line, refund, reroute forward or return are refused by the server for every role and channel; a partner hold ends only with the partner's clearance recorded, a screening hold only with Management's second look or a new clear screening (Lifecycle 2c).

One open external instruction per promise: while an instruction is instructed, acknowledged or of unknown outcome, a second instruction for the same promise is refused (partial unique index on the promise); an alternative payout or reroute starts only from an instruction closed as rejected or acknowledged as not executed, with the partner's reference (Lifecycle 2d).

WALLET_SCREENING.decision is write-once for every role and channel; a reject is lifted only by a new screening row decided by Management on a second look; no role has a right over a partner's own hold or freeze (Roles rule 11).
A flagged or breached rate version prices nothing and instructs nothing; a dormant partner pair prices nothing and accepts no collection or settlement line (Calculation 2a; Scenario Catalogue).

idempotency_key is unique and (source_type, source_id, event) is unique: a retried request returns the first result; the source state change, the transaction and its postings are written in one database transaction, and the instruction to a partner is committed before the partner is called or told (Ledger Posting Design rule 1b).

Every type-plus-id reference is checked against TYPE_REGISTRY: the type value exists, the id exists in the table the registry names, and a ledger source belongs to the transaction's project (ERD Appendix C).

Email OTP: one open code per quote issue; a code validates once and the decision is write-once; on a project with the switch on, no collection is recorded without an approved CUSTOMER_APPROVAL of the group's current issue, and no quote is sent for a sender whose approver address and chat group are not present and approved; a new issue or a change of the sender's address voids the open code (Lifecycle 2e).

A cloned project activates only when every copied configuration row has clone_confirmed_at set, every referenced version is the one in force on the activation date and every block's route is complete (Configuration Schema rule 15).

WALKS.name: Quote-first deal, end to end
steps: PROJECT
One arrangement with the client (CLIENT → PROJECT, D38). Its policies (quote freshness and validity, grace, fee treatment, settlement policy and exposure cap) govern everything below.
SENDER
Operator picks the sender. The receiver groups this sender may pay are listed in SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW.
RECEIVER_GROUP
The entitled group. One of its receivers’ accounts must hold an approved destination (DESTINATION_APPROVAL) with the chosen partner before the deal leaves Inquiry.
PARTNER_PAIR
Choosing partner × currency pair is part of pricing. Partner and partner entity are fixed per leg.
FEE_STRUCTURE
The versioned client-side fee for that partner × pair is stamped on the deal group.
RATE_COMPARISON
Created lazily for partner × pair × date by the first deal of the day.
MARKET_RATE
The market snapshot from the pair’s prioritised rate source.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The partner’s rate version for the day; the breach check may freeze the pair until Finance decides.
DEAL_GROUP
The client-facing instruction: pair as the sender sees it, sender rate, fee, reference. Every deal belongs to one; this one has a single leg.
DEAL

Leg 1, forward, funded by a collection. Priced once; sent / valid / grace timestamps and quote_hash recorded. A sender who asks for more time before expiry gets Finance-approved extensions, as many as needed, at the same price; after expiry a new deal group, which may be priced on the old rate by an approved override (D45).
QUOTE_PACKAGE

The rendered quote as sent: template version, channel, printed sender-facing figures, sent_at (starts validity) and the hash that becomes the leg’s quote_hash. A re-issue is a new row; a new price is a new deal group (D35).
DESTINATION_APPROVAL
Destination approval precedes collection: an approved account of the entitled group with this partner.
COLLECTION
Funds arrive in 1..n parts into a COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT of the leg’s partner entity (bank or wallet by kind); cash with instructions on the deal.
CONVERSION

The partner converts against the exact rate version. actual_out is booked rounded as the pair says; a dropped fraction stays as client dust, a round-up is NPL’s cost (D25); the receiver fee is taken here; NPL’s margin is captured now and never again at risk.
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
One balanced transaction; margin recognition is the only client → company ownership flip.
SETTLEMENT
Pays the balance, rounded as the pair says, from the partner’s holding through a SETTLEMENT_RAIL with a SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY narrative.
SETTLEMENT_LINE
One or many destination accounts. Paying a receiver in another group creates the offset in the same action.
CONFIRMATION
The receiver confirms the amount received: full or short.
SHORTFALL
If short, a shortfall opens against the receiver and is topped up by a later settlement.
BANK_FEE_EVENT
Post-confirmation true-up of expected vs actual bank fee: waived, carried forward or absorbed.

WALKS.name: Collect-first deal
steps: COLLECTION
Funds arrive before any quote. Attribution needs an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry (Q1); the sender is picked from the configured list.
DEAL_GROUP
Created with entry_mode collect_first; the sender is promised nothing.
DEAL
The single leg is born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; no quote clocks.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The rate version is taken at conversion rather than stamped at quote.
CONVERSION
Converted against that version; actual_out booked; margin captured.
SETTLEMENT
Then the same whole-unit settlement as any other deal.

WALKS.name: Rejected payout and return leg
steps: SETTLEMENT
USDT was converted to GBP at PT and paid out to the receiver’s account.
SETTLEMENT_RETURN

The receiving or intermediary bank rejects the transfer. The GBP returns to PT minus bank fees; the line’s outcome becomes returned and a reversing transaction puts the money back into the client’s balance.
BANK_FEE_EVENT
The bounce fee is booked as expected vs actual, waived (client) or absorbed (NPL) per the project’s treatment.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
With the line reversed, the group’s entitlement is restored. Option B stops here: the GBP stays in balance for later payouts to receivers in the same group; another group would be an approved offset.
DEAL

Option A: a return leg on the same deal group. leg_type return, funding_source returned_settlement, GBP → USDT at PT, priced at conversion. NPL’s original margin is untouched; the FX loss falls on the client’s funds.
FEE_DECISION
Markup on the return leg is applied or waived case by case, with an approver.
CONVERSION
The reverse conversion, owned by the return leg, using PT’s rate version for GBP → USDT.
RECEIVER
The destination is the sender_return receiver linked to the parent leg’s sender. Any other receiver needs Management approval, a reason, and a prior destination approval.
RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT
The sender’s USDT wallet is one of that receiver’s accounts; it is chosen at payout and need not be the wallet the sender paid from.
SETTLEMENT_LINE
The USDT goes out as an ordinary payout line to that account, clearing the entitlement its return leg credited to the parent leg’s group (v5.0, D13).

WALKS.name: Two-leg route via a deal group
steps: DEAL_GROUP
The sender wants INR → EUR. Ali can collect INR but cannot reach EUR, so the group will have two legs. The group holds the one price the sender saw.
DEAL
Leg 1: INR → USDT at Ali, forward, funded by the collection. Partner fixed per leg.
CONVERSION
Ali converts to USDT; margin on leg 1 is captured here.
RECEIVER
Jeton’s collection wallet is registered as a RECEIVER of kind partner_transit, so the hop is an ordinary payout.
SETTLEMENT
Ali pays the USDT to the transit receiver’s account. Entitlement passes through the transit group.
PARTNER_CONFIG
Leg 2 is a second DEAL on the same group at Jeton: USDT → EUR, funding_source prior_leg, no collection.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
Jeton’s rate version for USDT → EUR prices leg 2 at conversion.
SETTLEMENT_LINE
Jeton pays the EUR to the real receiver’s account. Margin across the route = group quote − both partner conversions.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
The entitled group’s tally reconciles once leg 2 converts and pays out.

WALKS.name: Ad-hoc balance conversion
steps: PROJECT_BALANCE
The client holds 5K SGD and 10K USDT at PT and must pay 15K USDT.
BALANCE_CONVERSION
Finance converts SGD → USDT at PT. Not a deal: no sender, receiver or collection. It names the group it serves (chosen split).
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The same rate procedure applies: partner rate version, market snapshot, breach check.
FEE_DECISION
Markup is optional, decided case by case with an approver.
CONVERSION
Owned by the balance conversion; actual_out rounded as the pair says, the residual kept as dust (D25).
ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION
The served group’s SGD entitlement becomes USDT entitlement. Any excess over its SGD entitlement is another group’s flow, booked as an approved offset.
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
Source BalanceConversion: debit client due USDT, credit client due SGD; an earnings posting only if markup was applied.
SETTLEMENT
The 15K USDT goes out as an ordinary settlement.

WALKS.name: Reroute, custody and recover dues
steps: DEAL
A priced leg hits a partner problem: unavailable, limit reached, holiday, compliance hold.
REROUTE

The only way the partner pair or partner entity changes after quote. Before collection, after collection or after conversion: after collection the outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender; after conversion the balance comes back through the own wallet to the alternate partner. Finance approves a reroute before conversion; Management approves one after conversion and ratifies every emergency action.
OWN_WALLET

Contingency custody. CL.OWN.*.HELD may be debited in four cases only (a reroute before conversion, the balance of a reroute after conversion, an own-desk leg, a bridge collection); custody_max_hours bounds it.
PARTNER_CONFIG
The alternate partner must have applicable_for_reroute set. NPL’s cut is captured at whichever partner converts, so nothing is withheld.
EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE

With forward_and_recover_dues, NPL forwards less than the full amount and reduces its receivable at that partner by the same figure: own wallet cash up, receivable down, no income. The partner’s agreement is recorded.
CUSTODY
The custody aging view (collections under open reroutes plus recovered dues resting in the wallet, minus forwarded) is the standing control.

WALKS.name: Rate day and breach approval
steps: RATE_SOURCE
Kraken, CMC, OANDA or XE, each with a staleness threshold.
PAIR_RATE_SOURCE
The prioritised source chain for each currency pair.
MARKET_RATE
Captured rate per source and pair; cross-source slippage is a query over these.
RATE_COMPARISON
One per partner × pair × date, with 2w and 4w average spreads built from confirmed versions only. A partner may give a new rate later the same day.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
Breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel). Quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze; Finance may also ask for a better rate.
APPROVAL
Finance approves with a reason or rejects. Approver ≠ initiator.
USER
Roles: ops, finance, management. Operations never sees derived-economics fields.

WALKS.name: Ledger and balances
steps: CONVERSION
A source event (collection, conversion, balance conversion, settlement, return, confirmation, bank fee event, reroute, markup share, rebate, loss event, adjustment).
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
One transaction per event, append-only; a correction is a reversing transaction.
LEDGER_POSTING
Debit and credit lines that sum to zero per currency, tagged client or company and by cost component.
LEDGER_ACCOUNT
Accounts coded OWNER.HOLDER.CCY.PURPOSE; client due balances are one account per project × partner × currency. ADVANCE no longer exists.
PROJECT_BALANCE
Conversions in, balance conversions across currencies, returns back in, settlements out. Never stored; carries dust below one unit.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
Per group and currency: forward legs’ client_net ± re-attributions − paid + returned. Σ groups = Σ client balance (invariant 7).
OFFSET
Positive = owed, negative = holding another group’s flow. Zero by construction in a single-group project.

DOC_META: NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline. Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model, Draft v6.1. New XP Technologies Limited, 28 October 2026, Confidential — internal baseline document; the client-facing documents of the P0 pack are derived from it and served without status, change-history, decision references, draft markers or edition numbers. Supersedes v5.9 (11 October), v5.8, v5.7, v5.6, v5.5, v5.4, v5.3, v5.2, v5.1, v5.0, v4.0 and v3.0 in full.
CONVENTIONS: All monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals.
Audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4: APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG, RECORD_LOCK) and apply to all master data.

Seven diagrams across four domains, one schema: 1a and 1b Configuration, 2 Rates, 3a and 3b Deal / collection / conversion / reroute, 3c Settlement / confirmation / fees / losses, 4 Ledger & controls.

Derived figures (client balance, entitlement, offsets, custody, invoice balance, month volume, client position, wallet registry, reporting values, reseller and remittance margins, NPL profit) are views over postings and deals — never stored.

Configuration: A Client is the commercial relationship; a Project is one arrangement with it (D38) and owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, destination approvals and rebate terms all hang off it.

Receivers belong to receiver groups only when kind = counterparty: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver is in exactly one group. sender_return (stands for a sender, for refunds via the ordinary payout path) and partner_transit (stands for a partner's collection endpoint, for the hop of a two-leg route) are group-less; they never appear on forward deals or allow lists, and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays it (v5.0, D13). Entitlement is tracked per group; only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
A receiving entity has one or more accounts, each with a currency and a rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). DESTINATION_APPROVAL and SETTLEMENT_LINE point at the account.

Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner’s markup is visible; PARTNER_PAIR.partner_fee_pct is known only for fee_on_market partners — otherwise partner cost is inferred through the rate comparison.

Collection endpoints live in one table (v5.1, D15): COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT under the partner entity, kind bank / wallet; cash-in has no record (instructions captured on the deal). The collected cash amount is rounded by the pair’s cash_rounding option to cash_rounding_unit (D25). An endpoint carries a nullable rail: a bank endpoint must have it before it becomes active, a wallet may leave it null and must match network when it is set (v5.2, D18); the endpoint’s kind must match the leg’s collection_method (v5.2, D19).

Destination approval is per partner: DESTINATION_APPROVAL is an account of the project’s receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying that partner’s approval status and payout details. The payout details follow the account’s kind: bank_details_ref for a bank account, network and address for a wallet (v5.2, D16).

SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it — neither holds money, neither is a ledger holder. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance — where the sender’s funds originated; reference only, never a payout destination.

OWN_WALLET exists for rerouting and pass-through (AQN-LT-Sub is an own wallet at Aquanow); PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY and MARKUP_SHARE_RULE record markup shares NPL pays; PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records rebates a partner pays NPL.

v5.3 adds the configuration behind NPL’s fee practice: FEE_TIER volume tiers per calendar month (D21), FEE_OVERRIDE with its own split (D20), customer-facing fee settings on FEE_STRUCTURE (D22), MARKUP_SHARE_RULE as a share of the net markup settled by the party (D26), PARTNER_REBATE_RULE with a basis and a scope (D27), an own-desk PARTNER_CONFIG for NPL-GR whose endpoints are NPL’s own wallets (D23), the partner’s bank cutoff on PARTNER with per-day extensions and early closes in PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE (D29), a rounding menu per pair (D25), single-use endpoints and accounts (D32) and WALLET_SCREENING (D31).

v5.3 (D34, D36): HOLIDAY rows under PARTNER are the dates behind every ‘next business day’; MESSAGE_TEMPLATE is the versioned wording of outgoing messages, with the fields a template may print — a quote template prints sender-facing figures only.

v5.4 (D38): CLIENT is the commercial relationship above PROJECT. BF, BF Sub and BF Withdrawal are three projects of one client; client-level balances, exposure, earnings and rebates are the CLIENT_POSITION roll-up, never stored.

v5.4 (D39, D40): a partner’s methods are declared on PARTNER.supported_methods and its cutoff is optional (none for Jeton or Aquanow); NPL’s own wallets have a role — contingency, own desk or collection bridge — and WALLET_REGISTRY lists every known address with its owner and role.
Rates: The rate comparison for the day is the object the operator flow creates “if not done already”: one per partner × pair × date, reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.

A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate (a better rate still outside the threshold needs approval). Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.
v5.3: a partner rate version stores the rate as quoted and its direction, and the normalised rate is derived (D28); cash pairs are priced per location (D30).
Deal lifecycle: Every deal belongs to a DEAL_GROUP, the client-facing instruction (pair as the sender sees it, sender rate, fee, reference, entry mode). A plain deal is a group of one leg; a two-partner route has two forward legs (leg 2 funded by leg 1); a rejected payout is unwound by a return leg funded by the SETTLEMENT_RETURN.

Entry modes: quote_first (sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late_decision), collect_first (born Collected with priced_at = conversion time) and estimate_first (indicative figure, priced at conversion).
Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg; only a REROUTE changes partner_pair_id or partner_entity_id.

Convert sub-modes: in partner_calculates, actual_out is what the partner did and is booked; expected_out is the engine’s figure; variance is the difference, an exception if beyond tolerance. The client net never changes. A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION.

The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion (Q6). Amounts are rounded at conversion by the pair’s option (D25): a dropped fraction stays client money in the balance and is paid when it reaches a unit; an amount added by rounding up is NPL’s cost. NPL’s margin is captured at conversion and is never at risk from a return or a forward.

One settlement model: SETTLEMENT drains one partner’s holding into one or many SETTLEMENT_LINEs, rounded as the pair says; under settlement_policy hold_allowed the balance may rest within the exposure cap. A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's is the offset, created by the same action; a line to a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group and is never an offset (v5.0). “Instant” is accumulate-one-then-settle-now.

BANK_FEE_EVENT is the post-confirmation true-up with expected vs actual, and books the bounce fee on a returned line. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved apply / waive / override of markup, network or bank fee on a single deal leg, settlement or balance conversion.

REROUTE forwards the full client amount or forwards and recovers dues (netting what the alternate partner owes NPL, within the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE, with the partner’s agreement recorded). Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.

v5.3: a leg stamps the override and tier that priced it, split across two tiers when it crosses a threshold (D20, D21); a deal group may pay an INVOICE and each payout line records how much of it was discharged and at what snapshot (D24); a leg records when the rate was locked, the cutoff that applied and when the conversion is due, and a bank-rail settlement records the cutoff and the day it may go out (D29); a cash part carries its token, agent and city (D30); a crypto part its sending address and screening (D31); a LOSS_EVENT reverses a part or a line, in full or in part, with the loss split across parties (D32).

v5.3 (D35): QUOTE_PACKAGE under DEAL_GROUP is the record of what was sent — template version, channel, printed figures, sent_at, hash. A quote-first leg is Sent only when a package has sent_at; re-issues are new rows; a new price is a new deal group.

v5.4 (D40, D41): a collection on a bridge wallet is forwarded to the leg’s partner as a hop within the wallet’s custody limit; on a cash settlement the receiver provides the token and the agent’s photo is the line’s evidence; covering a bank fee or exceeding the fee cap is recommended by Finance and approved by Management.

v5.5 (D45): a sender may ask for more time before a quote expires, as often as needed — each extension is a Finance-approved QUOTE_VALIDITY_EXTENSION row, Management added past the cutoff, the package re-issued at the same price; after expiry a new deal group, which at the sender’s request may be priced on the earlier leg’s rate by an approved override, the difference posting to variance. The price of a leg never moves; only its clock.

v5.7 (D46): fee parts are on the principal at the basis rate (client net = amount × rate × (1 − fee)); network fees are stated in USDT and absent when none applies; a cash collection is rounded to the pair’s cash unit at quote and the surplus over an invoice is the client’s.
Ledger & controls: Client money is kept as assets that say where it is — CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.COLLECTED, DUE, INTRANSIT, CL.OWN.<CCY>.HELD, CL.<RECEIVER>.<CCY>.SHORTFALL — and liabilities that say to whom NPL must deliver it: CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE (what NPL owes the client’s receivers, one account per currency) and CL.<SENDER>.<CCY>.CREDIT. Client assets equal client liabilities per currency; group entitlement is a view on the payable, not an account.

Company accounts: CO.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.POOL (NPL’s earnings resting at a partner), CO.OWN.<CCY>.WALLET (NPL’s own money in its wallet, e.g. recovered dues), REBATE_RECEIVABLE, SHARE_PAYABLE, and the income and expense accounts EARN_GROSS, EXP_PARTNER, EXP_BANKFEE, EXP_NETWORK, VARIANCE.
holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity: neither holds money. Project is a holder only for the PAYABLE.

Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver and nothing is withheld at source on a reroute; company → client postings exist only where NPL absorbs a fee or tops up a shortfall.

Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency; a conversion has an in-currency leg and an out-currency leg that each balance on their own. Corrections are reversing transactions that name what they reverse.

v5.3 account purposes: EARN_REBATE keeps rebate income apart from EARN_GROSS (D27); SHARE_RECEIVABLE holds NPL’s remainder owed by a party that keeps the converted funds (D26); EXP_ROUNDING takes the cost of rounding up (D25); EXP_LOSS takes NPL’s share of a loss event (D32). New transaction source LossEvent; new cost components rebate, share, fx_timing, cutoff_timing, loss. Own-desk deals (NPL-GR) use the ordinary partner-coded accounts with the own-desk configuration as holder, EXP_PARTNER zero by construction, and appear in the custody view (D23).

v5.4 (D43): the reporting currency (SYSTEM_SETTING) gives every aggregate one unit — project or overall collection volumes, earnings and rebates, current balances, custody — through REPORTING_VALUE, an estimate at the latest market rate of a system reporting pair, carrying the rate it used and a stale flag. Display only: nothing converted is ever posted or used to price or settle; the one control that reads it is a client exposure ceiling stated in that currency.

v5.4 (D44): one system-settings area — SYSTEM_SETTING keys, ROLE rows for user roles, and platform-scope currency pairs priced through PAIR_RATE_SOURCE; the reporting rate source is not a separate key.

v5.4 (D44): rights are rows, not text — ROLE_RIGHT holds, per role and controlled action, whether the role may initiate, may approve and which role is added on escalation; invariant 9 is checked against it.

v5.7 (D46): variances by cause — VAR_CONVERSION (the partner did something other than expected, and basis variance on a reroute), VAR_CUTOFF (D29), VAR_RATE_HONOUR (D45), VAR_FX_TIMING (an obligation priced on one day and discharged on another, D24); each can be a gain or a loss.

Commissions received by NPL (§4.2b): some partners rebate part of their fee (Jeton charges 1.25% and gives back 0.4%); tracked and reconciled monthly, paid back usually in crypto. A Partner Commissions report is required.

A partner may give a new rate during the day, so the same pair can have several PARTNER_RATE_VERSION rows on one date. On a breach Finance may also ask for a better rate; a better rate outside the threshold still needs finance/management approval.

Conversion direction: quote-first deals convert “conversion-needed currency >> collection currency” (sender asks for a target value); collect-first deals always convert “collection currency >> conversion currency”.
Besides a fixed upfront quote, NPL may give an estimate and convert after collection completes.
Receiver-side fee must be computed at conversion and balance attribution, otherwise the balance is incorrect.

Pass-through / double conversions (§7.1.1): when a partner can collect a currency but not convert to the target, NPL collects in an interim pair and sends the converted currency to a second partner (collect INR>USDT at Ali, USDT>AED at Jeton); ideally grouped as one transaction. A second scenario routes USDT via NPL’s own wallet when the partner lacks a banking channel (NPL acting as its own remittance client; probably out of scope).
Partner cost is deducted at transaction level; there is no cost accumulation paid later.

UNDERSTANDING:
NPLify — Project Understanding
Everything we currently understand about NPL’s remittance operations and the platform to be built · v1.0
New XP Technologies Limited
2 October 2026 · Working document · Confidential
How to read this. This is the consolidated understanding at the end of the first understanding block. It supersedes earlier drafts wherever they disagree (the ERD v2.1 and the P0 pack D2–D8 will be rebuilt from this document). §12 lists what changed along the way and why, so nothing that was corrected can quietly resurface. §11 lists what is still open. Nothing here is built; this is the thing we build from.
1 · What NPL does
NPL is a remittance coordinator. On behalf of its clients it arranges for money to be collected from payers, converted between currencies and rails (fiat and crypto — USDT most often), and settled to the right recipients. It does this through partners (Ali, Jeton, etc.) who do the actual conversion and hold or move the funds; NPL designs the deal, picks the partner, instructs, verifies and reconciles.
In terms of the partners, these are either remittance companies, Fintech, EMIs, Neobanks, Crypto Exchange (or a combination of these). For e.g. Ali has a few licensed remittance companies (referred to as PT – e.g. PT Global, PT Sukses, etc.). Jeton is a fintech which has a couple of different EMIs/Neobank offerings. When NPL uses a partner for a specific project, most often the facilitating entity/channel(s) are defined clearly (For e.g. Evo project via Ali will use PT Sukses).
Sometimes establishing the channel may require additional agreements between the partner/channel and the client (out of scope for NPL operations, managed at the NPL leadership level). In general, the client relationships are ring-fenced from the partners & vice-versa, so for the business to continue, NPL’s involvement is always required (meaning the partner doesn’t have any interaction with the client – all communication flows through NPL).
NPL’s income is the margin engineered into the price it quotes. Everything else in the platform — rates, fees, ledgers, offsets, approvals — exists to compute that margin, protect it, and prove it.
Today the whole operation runs on spreadsheets, messaging channels and people’s memories. The platform replaces that with a configuration-driven engine that reproduces today’s calculations exactly first, then takes over.
2 · Principles that bind everything
No custody in the normal path. Client money flows sender → partner → recipient. NPL’s own wallet is used only under a recorded, approved reroute when the intended partner cannot handle the volume (§7.1).
Priced once. A deal’s rate and fees are stamped at one moment and never recomputed (there are exceptions such as the customer makes a transfer after the rate duration expired, customer asked for a better rate, etc. – finance/management approval needed). In quote-first deals that moment is the quote; in collect-first deals it is the conversion.
Immutable, double-entry ledger. Every movement is a balanced pair of postings; nothing is edited or deleted; corrections are reversing entries; every balance is a sum, never a stored field.
Whose money is always known. Every amount carries an owner tag: client funds or company earnings. The partner’s share is a cost line, not a pot NPL holds.
Disburse to zero. A client balance exists only because the next settlement has not happened yet. NPL never sits on client funds by choice; deliberate partial settlement or reserves are not normal behavior. For some clients with a higher balance threshold in which case the balances sit with the partner until settled.
Nobody approves their own work; Operations never sees margins. Three cumulative roles, maker-checker on every controlled action, derived economics visible only to Finance and Management.
The FRS flow is one configuration. The Client 1 USDT→EUR flow described in the FRS must be expressible as data in this model, and must reproduce Appendix A’s figures.
3 · Configuration model
A Project is the top-level container — from the system’s point of view the project is the client (the client name is a label). A project’s Configuration has four kinds of content.
3.1 System settings (thresholds)
Max amount; system validations; frequency (daily settlement slots); rate-variation tolerances between market and agent (partner); custom conditions as the project-specific catch-all. All versioned, Finance proposes, Management approves.
3.2 Currency pairs
The project’s master list of what it trades, each with a quoting direction (units of OUT per IN, or IN per OUT), precision (5 dp standard; 8 dp for sub-unit pairs such as USDT→BTC), and the reference-rate source chain for that pair.
Note – for cash collections, the cash currency is always rounded off to the nearest 100, 500 or 1000 units (depending on the currency value). For e.g. INR is rounded to nearest 1000, SGD, USD is rounded to nearest 100
3.3 Receivers and senders (project level, partner-independent)
A Receiver is a counterparty on the receiving side and is the group: a party with one or more receiving entities (Receiver X → Entity X1, Entity X2; Receiver Y → VoiceAIWrapper). Receiving entities carry name and bank details.
A Sender is a single paying party (Sender A, Sender B) with a sendable_to allow-list naming which receiver(s) their money may go to (Sender A → Receiver Y only; Sender B → Receiver X only). One receiver is the common case; the model allows a list.
There is an exception where the funds could be “temporarily” sent to another receiver (within the same project/client) and then reclaimed when new collections for the other receiver/group are done – referenced in 6.3
Senders and receivers are not tied to a partner: the same Sender A → Receiver Y flow may run through Ali today and Jeton tomorrow.
3.4 Partner configuration (one block per partner, within the project)
How a given partner is used in this project:
---
Element | Meaning
Currency pair(s) | Which of the project’s pairs this partner handles
Fees | NPL’s client-side fee for this partner × pair (see §4)
Facilitating entities/Channel | The partner’s legal vehicles (Ali → PT-tour, PT Global Inc, …); name, optional bank details
Collection - Wallet configuration | Crypto-in endpoints (wallets per facilitating entity / network)
Collection — receiving entities | Bank-in endpoints on the partner side (name, bank details)
Collection — sending entities | Provenance reference: the actual account the sender’s funds originate from (their own bank account or one of their clients’). Reference only — says where the money came from, does not change the sender or the destination
Settlement — receiving entities | The project’s receiving entities registered with this partner (NewXP under Ali, NewXP under Jeton …) carrying that partner’s approval status and the bank details it pays to. Destination approval is therefore per partner

---
Collection endpoints are three kinds by method: crypto-in → wallet, bank-in → collection receiving entity, cash-in → nothing pre-configured (instructions are issued at transaction time).
4 · Pricing model
4.1 How partners disclose their price
A partner either (a) gives NPL a rate with its markup already inside it, or (b) states market + x%. In case (b) the partner’s cost is explicit; in case (a) it is invisible and must be inferred by comparing the partner’s rate with market references.
4.2 How NPL prices the client
NPL’s markup sits on either the partner rate + x% or market + x%, where NPL’s x% is larger than the partner’s so the margin survives. The fee is set per partner × currency pair — the same USDT→EUR flow is priced differently to the client depending on whether Ali or Jeton handles it. Choosing the partner is therefore part of pricing.
Fee parameters per partner × pair: basis (market | partner), total percentage, split between sender and receiver (sender’s share is embedded in the sender rate; receiver’s share is deducted from the client-net), mode fixed | variable, and per-sender overrides (may be zero).
Variable mode sets the fee to protect a margin floor against the partner’s current spread, within a floor and a cap; a quote that cannot reach the floor proceeds only with Finance approval (“below-margin”).
The one unknown in the model: when NPL prices on market + x% but the partner priced style (a), NPL’s realised margin = NPL’s x% minus the partner’s hidden markup. The variance history exists for this, and the minimum-margin check must be live at conversion, not only assumed at quote.
4.2a NPL paying Referral Commissions:
Sometimes NPL has to pay referral commissions to external markup-share parties who brought in the client. This can involve a) sharing the NPL’s earnings in a predetermined ratio OR b) a fixed % for each party involved. There could also be multiple people involved in the same deal. E.g.
Scenario 1 - John brought a new client and expects to get 1% fixed on each transaction. NPL can keep its fee fixed or variable but has to apply john’s 1% into the sender-facing rate.  So, if the fee structure is of partner rate + markup, then markup will include NPL’s fee + john’s 1%
Scenario 2 – John and James are 2 parties that want a share of the earnings. NPL decides to markup 0.5% for itself, 0.25% for john and 0.25% for james.
4.2b NPL getting commissions:
In some cases (e.g. Evo project via Jeton), they give back a % of the fee they charge on the transaction. So if Jeton charges 1.25%, they give back 0.4% back from that fee. This needs to be tracked and reconciled (summary of all transactions, fees generated, expected commissions) every month. After the reconciliation, Jeton would pay this commission back to NPL (via crypto usually).
4.3 Rates, comparison and variance
Reference rate per pair from a source chain (Kraken → CoinMarketCap for crypto pairs; Oanda/XE as adapters for fiat), snapshotted at the pricing moment with source and time. Multiple sources per pair make cross-source slippage (XE vs Oanda vs Kraken) a tracked quantity, not a surprise.
A rate comparison for the day (partner × pair) is created lazily by the first deal that needs it and reused by every deal that day. It records the partner’s rate version, the market snapshot, the spread, and the rolling 2-week / 4-week average of confirmed spreads. Occasionally the partner may give a new rate for the day, so same pair may have different versions on the same day.
A partner rate whose spread exceeds the rolling average by more than the configured relative tolerance is breached: quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a recorded reason or rejects (or asks for a better rate). Better rate doesn’t guarantee that the new rate will be under the threshold, and if it’s outside the threshold, then finance/management approval is needed. No skip path.
Partner rate versions are never overwritten; a conversion always references the exact version it used.
5 · The deal
5.1 Two entry modes
---
| Quote → Collect → Convert | Collect → Convert
What happens | Sender wants a target outcome (1,000 USD); the quote works backwards (≈ 1,004 USDT at 0.4 %); sender pays the quoted amount | Sender simply sends (1,000 USDT); NPL converts at the then-current rate and fee (996 USD)
Pricing moment | Quote | Conversion
What’s promised | Exact in and exact out | Nothing — amount out follows the rate at conversion
Who bears rate movement | NPL (hence validity, grace and drift clocks) | The sender
Lifecycle entry | Inquiry → Quoted → Accepted → Collecting | Born at Collected
Mode | Target-out (or fixed-in) | Always fixed-in
Direction of conversion pair | Sender would ask for specific value conversion. So if the pair is USDT-EUR, the conversion direction will be EUR>>USDT (i.e. “conversion needed currency” >> “collection currency”) | Conversion direction is always “collection currency” >> “conversion currency”
---
There is another scenario where instead of a fixed “upfront quote”, NPL gives an estimate. And then the conversion is done after the collection is completed.
5.2 Building the deal (operator flow)
Sender selected → the receiver from sendable_to is shown (display only; the entity within it is chosen at settlement).
Currency pair selected → partners configured for that pair → partner chosen → fee structure for partner × pair applies automatically → mode chosen (quote-first / collect-first) → the rate the fee basis needs is entered (partner rate or market rate) → the day’s rate comparison is created if it does not exist.
Facilitating entity of the chosen partner selected → its wallet / bank details / cash instructions become the “address” in the message.
Draft message for the customer: calculation (quote-first), address, references. Partner and facilitating entity are therefore fixed at quote time; only a reroute changes them.
Collection: hash / slip / receipt verified → status changes. Parts are allowed (80K today, 20K tomorrow). Overpayment → sender credit; underpayment → wait, or void with disposition.
Convert, in one of two sub-modes: NPL calculates and instructs the partner, or the partner calculates and NPL verifies. In the second, the partner’s actual figure is what is booked; the engine’s expectation is the comparison; the difference is variance, and an exception opens if beyond tolerance. The deal does not wait — the money already moved.
Settlement (§6).
5.3 Quote clocks and the late decision
Freshness (package must be marked sent within minutes of the snapshot) → validity (per client, e.g. 60 min) → grace (e.g. 15 min, only if market drift ≤ 0.10 %) → late decision: either re-quote at today’s rate with a fresh deal reference, or — if the project’s policy allows — honour the old rate as a relationship call with recorded Finance approval. The original quote stamp never changes; only the decision to accept against it does.
5.4 Destination approval
For destinations that need the partner’s approval, approval happens before collection: the route is approved, NPL confirms money can reach the destination, and only then collects. Never hold what you cannot deliver.
6 · Settlement, balances and offsets
6.1 The client balance is per partner
After conversion, funds sit with the partner that converted them. The ledger keeps one due balance per (client × partner × currency); the client-level balance is the sum across partners and is never stored
6.2 One settlement model
Accumulate (a balance exists) → settle (the balance goes to zero; one settlement may split across one or several destinations) → receiver confirms → fee adjustments per project. “Instant” settlement is simply accumulate-one-deal-then-settle-now; there is one path with a timing policy, not two modes.
A settlement draws from one partner’s holding and goes out through that partner’s settlement sending entity (narrative) via its facilitating entity (rail) to receiving entities registered with that partner. Emptying the client balance may take one settlement per partner that holds something; a residual at Jeton while Ali is at zero is still a non-zero balance.
6.3 Entitlement and offsets
sendable_to says whose flow a collection belongs to; the converted money nonetheless lands in the shared client balance. So receiver entitlement is a tracking layer on the balance: “of this balance, Receiver X’s flow accounts for X, Receiver Y’s for Y.”
Offsets are arithmetic on that layer, not movements of money:
Tier 1 — within a receiver: NPL’s money cannot reach NewXP, so it is paid to ReferScout (also NPL’s). Entitlement unchanged; the tally records which of NPL’s entities holds which share.
Tier 2 — across receivers: only when every entity of a receiver is blocked is its flow paid to another receiver (Receiver X → Receiver Y). The tally shows a receiver holding more than its entitlement.
Both are the same number — entitlement − paid per receiver — and clear as later settlements favour whoever is behind. Tier 2 is the heavier event (money with a party it does not belong to) and carries higher approval and tighter aging.
A settlement that crosses receivers creates the tier-2 figure in the same action; nobody has to remember to record it.
6.4 Fee adjustments at settlement
Receiver-side fee (the 0.60 %-style share): computed before settlement because it determines the amount sent. This should be computed at the time of conversion and balance attribution. Otherwise, the balance will be incorrect, if the receiver side fee is only deducted at the time of settlement.
Bank / payout fees: a true-up after confirmation, per the project’s treatment:
---
Treatment | Example (we send €8,500; bank takes €50)
Waived | Client receives €8,450 and does not ask for it back — fee on the client; memo only
Carry-forward | Client receives €8,450 and asks for it next time — NPL owes €50, added to the next settlement
Absorbed (gross-up) | NPL expects the €50 and sends €8,550 so the client nets €8,500 — NPL’s cost. Expected vs actual difference is tracked, never lost
---
Default per client, overridable per settlement with approval.
7 · Exceptions
7.1 Rerouting (the only time NPL holds funds)
When the partner intended to handle the volume is unavailable (outage, limit reached, holiday, compliance hold), a deal is moved onto a pre-approved contingency route: collection into NPL’s own wallet, onward to an alternate partner from the project’s applicable set. Rerouting is a controlled action (Ops requests, Finance approves, reason recorded).
On a rerouted deal NPL chooses what to forward: the full amount (partner converts everything; earnings settle back later), withhold its own earnings at source, or withhold and recover dues — earnings from earlier direct deals still parked at that partner, recovered by short-paying the partner now. Eligibility for withholding depends on route, partner, sender risk and other criteria Finance will define. Recovery is an asset moving from the partner’s wallet to NPL’s, never new income, and every deduction names the deal it recovers.
When the alternate partner is chosen at conversion time and NPL’s fee rides on the partner rate, the quote was priced on a quoting-basis rate (default: the worst applicable partner rate) and the gap to the actual partner rate posts as basis variance on earnings, with the margin floor re-checked.
Custody position for NPL sign-off: NPL’s wallet holds client funds only under a recorded reroute; every resting balance has a deal, a reason and an age; outbound transfers from NPL’s wallet are dual-approved (Finance + Management) and executed by NPL signers outside the platform (hardware or multisig). The regulatory posture of contingency holding is for NPL’s counsel.
7.1.1 Pass-through / Double Conversions:
There are occasions where the route is not a direct one – meaning the partner can collect a currency but can’t convert to the expected currency. In such cases, NPL requests the collection to be done in an interim currency pair and then sends the resulting/converted currency to a different route/partner. E.g. the client wants NPL to collect INR and settle in AED. Ali can collect INR>USDT, but not AED, so the converted USDT is sent to Jeton who is able to send USDT>AED - (this is not a real example just an illustration). While this can be handled as 2 different transactions, it would be good to see if we can group it into a single transaction.
Another scenario is that the sender wants NPL to collect INR and pay EUR to vendors (receivers). However, Ali doesn’t have an available banking channel for these transfers. The vendor/receiver can however receive USDT. NPL can either a) ask Ali to settle the USDT direct to the client OR b) ask Ali to pay into NPL’s wallet and NPL then sends the outgoing transfer from its own wallet. This scenario is real and applicable in cases where NPL is reselling certain gaming solutions (in essence NPL is acting as its own remittance client). – probably out of scope from remittance platform standpoint/to be reviewed.

Situation | Handling
Quote expires | §5.3 late decision
Deal voided before money | State change with reason; no ledger postings
Deal voided after collection | Refund (network-fee policy to decide), or funds kept as sender credit, or hold — Management approves the disposition

Destination blocked (holiday, in-transit) | §6.3 offsets — same receiver’s other entities first, another receiver only if all are blocked

8 · Money ownership and the ledger
Client funds: everything from collection to confirmed delivery. NPL coordinates, never owns.
Company earnings: the only money in NPL’s own accounts. Recognised at conversion: the sender’s stamped price fixes the client-net; whatever remains after converting exactly the client-net is NPL’s gross margin, which physically rests at the partner as a pool (the FRS’s “PT Comms” residual). That pool is NPL’s earnings receivable at that partner.
Partner cost: deducted from the pool on the partner’s fee cycle. Total cost to the client = partner cost + NPL’s earnings, and both are sums over postings carrying a cost component (earnings, partner_cost, bank_fee, network_fee, variance). The partner cost is deducted at transaction level (there is no cost accumulation or total cost paid later, etc.
Ownership flips from client to company at exactly three events: margin recognition at conversion; withholding at source on a rerouted deal; an advance to a receiver (company money paid ahead, repaid as entitlement accrues).
Shortfalls (confirmed-short deliveries) are tracked and topped up on the next settlement, funded from the pool.
Standing identities checked daily: client due per partner = Σ receiver entitlements; pool per partner = partner-stated comms balance ± logged difference; exposure (due + in-transit) ≤ policy; own-wallet holdings = 0 unless an open reroute; offsets = Σ (entitlement − paid); each confirmation = its in-transit amount exactly.
9 · Roles and controls
Operations quotes, verifies, prepares, instructs. Sees operational fields, sender-facing prices and partner rates as entered. Never sees reference rate at capture, spread, margin, comms, cost breakdown, ledgers or earnings — on any screen, export, message or report.
Finance sees all of that, approves what Ops initiates (quotes, rates, conversions, settlements, exceptions), owns reconciliation and the Finance Log.
Management sees everything, approves escalations: settlements above limit, third same-day slot, advances, offset redirections, shortfall top-ups, contingency routes, own-wallet outbound (mandatory), configuration changes, user changes, post-money voids. Countersigns releases when only one Finance user is on shift.
Visibility is cumulative (Ops ⊂ Finance ⊂ Management); gating is server-side; approver ≠ initiator is enforced at the endpoint; every controlled action is audited with actor, time, reason and record version.
Identity: Google Workspace SSO only.
10 · Reporting and reconciliation
Finance Log is the reporting spine: every posting, every approval, time-travel to any past moment because nothing was edited.
Daily reconciliation: platform vs partner statements vs bank slips; breaks become logged exceptions; small persistent gaps (rounding, partner charges) accumulate as shortfalls topped up monthly.
Calculation-comparison reports during test runs: system-computed figures beside the spreadsheet’s, per deal and per identity.
Custody aging report: every balance in NPL’s wallet by deal, reason and hours since collection.
Partner Commissions report for reconciliation (referenced in 4.2b)

D1 receiver groups (design F): project → receiver group → receiver → receiving entity → account; one default group per project; entitlement per group; offsets only across groups; a single group has no offset; reason: payouts within a pot are ordinary settlement, new receiving entities weekly need no re-attribution; alternatives rejected: project flag, separate projects per pot, receiver pooling by self-reference, attribution to sender, per-deal buckets. D3 receiver kinds: counterparty / sender_return (stands for a sender) / partner_transit (stands for a partner endpoint); keeps one payout path and partner destination approval; refund destination account chosen at payout, not tied to provenance wallet; third-party refund only with Management approval, reason and pre-registered receiver; sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less (v5.0 D13 removed the v4.0 return group), never on forward deals or allow lists; rejected: SENDER_ACCOUNT and a widened destination. D4 balance conversion as its own action (BALANCE_CONVERSION), not a leg: no sender/receiver/collection, Finance-initiated, may serve several payouts; chosen-group split with ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION; a CONVERSION has exactly one owner. D5 FEE_DECISION: one-off apply/waive/override with approver for markup on return legs and balance conversions, network-fee override (Q7), bank-fee override. D6 SETTLEMENT_RETURN and a returned outcome on the line; reversing posting; bounce fee via BANK_FEE_EVENT. D7 RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (Q4).
